key_insight: The paper shows that instead of running expensive reinforcement learning directly on a large target model, you can train a smaller model with RLVR and transfer that learned improvement to the stronger model through direct on-policy distillation. This creates a practical weak-to-strong path for boosting reasoning without repeating costly rollouts at full scale.
problem_solved: It addresses the high cost and scaling bottleneck of post-training large language models with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, where the target model must repeatedly generate many rollouts during training.
method: Run RLVR on a smaller, cheaper "weak" model to learn improved reasoning behavior.
Use direct on-policy distillation to transfer the post-RL behavior from the weak model to a stronger target model.
Reuse the learned signal from one RL run to avoid repeating expensive RL training on every new strong model.
impact: This matters because it reduces the compute and rollout cost of post-training while still improving a larger model's reasoning. For practitioners, it offers a more scalable recipe for upgrading strong models using cheaper training runs.

paper_title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Shiyuan Feng, Huan-ang Gao, Haohan Chi, Hanlin Wu, Zhilong Zhang
